hollow: fāʿil and mafʿūl look identical (مُكْتَالٌ); jussive نَكْتَلْ (12:63)
doubled: fāʿil and mafʿūl look identical (مُلْتَفٌّ); amr also اِلْتَفِفْ
Form VIII of ن ث ر (not Form VII)
Form VIII of ن ه ي (not Form VII); الْمُنْتَهَى = the final end (53:42)
wāw assimilated into the tā': اِوْتَسَقَ → اِتَّسَقَ
wāw assimilated into the tā': اِوْتَقَى → اِتَّقَى; the noun تَقْوَى is from the same root
wāw assimilated into the tā' (اِوْتَكَأَ → اِتَّكَأَ); مُتَّكَأٌ = couch/banquet (12:31)
both مُسْتَقِرٌّ (fāʿil) and مُسْتَقَرٌّ (place of settling) occur in the Qur'an
hollow: maṣdar takes tā' (اِسْتِقَامَة); amr اِسْتَقِمْ
maṣdar: wāw becomes yā' after kasra (اِسْتِيفَاء)
past passive اُسْتُوقِنَ: sākin yā' after ḍamma becomes wāw

en: to exceed all bounds, be insolent
note: used with عَنْ (عَتَوْا عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ); عَاتِيَة (69:6) = raging beyond bounds

en: to be empty, hollow, in ruins
note: lafīf maqrūn like طَوَى يَطْوِي: the middle wāw stays sound
الْمُؤْتَفِكَات = the overturned cities (of Lūṭ's people); when starting, اِئْتَفَكَ is pronounced ītafaka
Form I خَطِئَ = to sin wilfully (خَاطِئ); Form IV أَخْطَأَ = to err unintentionally
lafīf mafrūq like وَقَى يَقِي: the imperative is the single letter هِ (هِهْ in pause)
also 'to be alone with' when used with إِلَى
present also يَحْجِزُ
used with إِلَى (مُهْطِعِينَ إِلَى الدَّاعِ)
hollow: maṣdar takes tā' (إِبَانَة); also intransitive 'to be clear', so مُبِين = clear / making plain
opposite of Form IV أَقْسَطَ 'to act justly'

en: to turn aside to, seek refuge
note: مُلْتَحَدًا (72:22) is the ẓarf: a place of refuge
الْمُزَّمِّلُ = الْمُتَزَمِّلُ with the tā' assimilated into the zāy
نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ (73:6) = rising (for prayer) at night
73:8 pairs the Form V verb تَبَتَّلْ with this Form II maṣdar تَبْتِيلًا
مَهِيل is the contracted ism al-mafʿūl of a hollow-yā' verb (from مَهْيُول)

en: to wrap oneself in a cloak
note: الْمُدَّثِّرُ = الْمُتَدَثِّرُ with the tā' assimilated into the dāl
here intransitive (= نَفَرَ); also used transitively 'to put to flight, call to arms'
also نَضِرَ يَنْضَرُ and نَضُرَ يَنْضُرُ; maṣdar نَضْرَة in 76:11, 83:24
فَاقِرَة (75:25) = a back-breaking calamity; unrelated in sense to فَقُرَ / اِفْتَقَرَ 'to be poor'
التَّرَاقِيَ (75:26) is really the plural of تَرْقُوَة 'collarbone'; the corpus tags it a Form VI maṣdar, matching تَرَاقَى (root ر ق ي) — this ṣarf is theoretical
hollow: maṣdar takes tā' (اِسْتِطَارَة)
وِلْدَانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ = youths kept forever young
present also يَنْثِرُ
imperative اِيثَمْ (from اِئْثَمْ, the second hamza becoming yā')
كِفَاتًا (77:25) is usually explained from Form I كَفَتَ يَكْفِتُ 'to draw together'; this Form III is theoretical
distinct from نَشِطَ يَنْشَطُ نَشَاطًا 'to be lively'
assimilated: wāw drops in the present and imperative (يَجِفُ، جِفْ)
مُرْسَاهَا (79:42) = its fixed time of arrival (ẓarf)
assimilated + hamzated: wāw drops (يَئِدُ), imperative إِدْ like عِدْ
doubled root, but Form II keeps all three radicals
used with إِلَى (كَادِحٌ إِلَى رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا)

en: to come by night; to knock
note: الطَّارِق (86:1) = the night-comer (the star)
of a star (ثُقُوبًا) it is intransitive: to blaze, pierce the dark
مَاءٍ دَافِقٍ (86:6): 'gushing', or fāʿil in the sense of مَدْفُوق; present also يَدْفِقُ
يُحْمَى عَلَيْهَا (9:35) is its impersonal passive; distinct from حَمَى يَحْمِي 'to protect'
imperative also اُصْفُفْ
imperative also اُبْثُثْ
quadriliteral-like pattern فَيْعَلَ (mulḥaq), not a true Form II; the Qur'an writes it with ṣād: مُصَيْطِر
أَكْلًا لَمًّا (89:19) = devouring everything; imperative also اُلْمُمْ
quadriliteral Form IV (اِفْعَلَلَّ) of root ط م أ ن; imperative also اِطْمَأْنِنْ
maṣdar عَيْلَة in 9:28; distinct from عَالَ يَعُولُ 'to provide for'
hollow root, but the wāw is sound in Form II
also سَفُلَ and سَفِلَ
usually with عَلَى; also transitive: مَا كَذَبَ الْفُؤَادُ مَا رَأَى (53:11), وَعْدٌ غَيْرُ مَكْذُوبٍ (11:65)
مُنْفَكِّينَ (98:1) = desisting/departing; imperative also اِنْفَكِكْ
used with عَلَى; hollow: maṣdar takes tā' (إِغَارَة); lexicons list it under غ و ر
intransitive in نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ الْقَوْمِ (21:78): to stray grazing at night
التَّكَاثُرُ (102:1) is strictly the maṣdar of Form VI تَكَاثَرَ يَتَكَاثَرُ 'to vie with one another in increase'
first radical wāw: يُوْقِدُ is written يُوقِدُ, maṣdar إِيقَاد
doubled root, but Form II keeps all three radicals

en: to bring to nothing, lead astray
note: فِي تَضْلِيلٍ (105:2) = (their plot) brought to ruin; doubled root keeps all radicals in Form II
آلَفَ = أَأْلَفَ, maṣdar إِيلَاف = إِئْلَاف (106:1–2)
used with عَنْ (عَنْ صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ)
also شَنَأَ يَشْنَأُ; maṣdar شَنَآن in 5:2, 5:8
مِفْتَاحٌ (a key) is the instrument noun in everyday use; the Qur'an has its plural مَفَاتِحُ (6:59)
hollow verb (ذَوَقَ → ذَاقَ), like قَالَ يَقُولُ; the Qur'an uses it for tasting punishment — فَذُوقُوا (78:30) — and mercy alike
Form V of كَلَّمَ (to speak to someone); negated in 78:38 — لَا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ

en: to turn toward, give one's attention to
note: takes لِ (تَصَدَّى لَهُ); in 80:6 it is the present تَتَصَدَّى with one tāʾ dropped
hollow Form IV like أَقَامَ: the maṣdar إِمَاتَة makes up its lost letter with tāʾ marbūṭah; paired with أَحْيَا throughout the Qur'an
Form I قَبَرَ = to bury; Form IV أَقْبَرَ = to provide a grave — فَأَقْبَرَهُ (80:21)
Form I نَشَرَ = to spread; Form IV = to bring the dead back to life — أَنشَرَهُ (80:22); نُشُورٌ = the Resurrection (67:15)
doubled verb: the two qāfs merge (شَقَّ) but part before a consonant ending — شَقَقْنَا (80:26); imperative also اُشْقُقْ; مَشَقَّةٌ (hardship) is the same root
